svg.title: The five modules and which stage of the flow each one owns
svg.desc: A hand-drawn map of the build's modules. The ingest module owns the offline phase: read, chunk, header, embed, and index, everything that happens once per corpus change, with the chunk header being one cheap cached LLM call per chunk. The retrieve module owns dense and sparse search, reciprocal rank fusion, and cross-encoder reranking, where the reranker is the single largest quality lever. The prompt module owns the five-block system prompt and bookend packing with citation tags, where order is a decision rather than an accident of ranking. The chat module owns the turn loop and is thin on purpose, because logic living there is logic the eval cannot reach. Two panels below cover the eval module, which wraps the online phase in a scorer by calling it rather than re-implementing it, and the llm module, which holds the header model, the generator, and the embedding client together.
svg.text: Five modules, mapped one-to-one onto the flow
Which file owns which stage is the most useful thing to know before opening any of them.

Wraps the online phase in a scorer. It does not re-implement the
pipeline; it calls it, which is what makes the gate meaningful.
One place for the model clients: the cheap header model, the
generator, and the embedding client, all configured together.
Out of scope by choice: streaming UI, multi-tenant auth, GraphRAG, fine-tuning, distributed indexing. Extensions, not foundations.
The core works without any of them, which is the point of building it in this order.
